hints: During one left-to-right round, a value can move left by at most one position.
After k rounds, the next output value can come from at most the next k+1 remaining positions.
Keep those candidates in a min-heap, breaking ties by original order.
analogy: Imagine repeatedly selecting the smallest card from a window of k+1 cards and then revealing one new card.
example: For [3,2,4,1,4] and k=2, a heap of the next three values first selects 2, then 1, producing [2,1,3,4,4].
algorithm: Insert the first min(n,k+1) pairs (value,original index) into a min-heap. Repeatedly extract and output the smallest pair, then insert the next unseen pair if any. Compare indices to preserve order among equal values. If k is at least n, the heap contains all elements and the result is the stable sorted array.
correctness: A value moves left by at most one position per round, so among the remaining values only the first k+1 can occupy the next position. Bubble passes move the smallest of these candidates left across all larger predecessors, while equal values retain order. Once that first position is fixed, the same argument applies inductively to the remainder.
complexity: For n elements, time is O(n log(min(n,k+1))) and space O(min(n,k+1)).
